tagline: Australia's canal-and-Broadwater lifestyle city — dense waterway network plus the Brisbane and Stradbroke edges.
summary: The Gold Coast is built around the Broadwater and one of the world's largest networks of residential canals, with a heavy marina, charter and waterfront-lifestyle market (Marina Mirage, Sanctuary Cove). Water connects the city's spine, and the Brisbane (~40 nm) and Stradbroke Island links extend it. All core legs are inside Pioneer II range. This is a strong charter and waterway-mobility starter with commuter upside on the Brisbane corridor.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Pioneer II covers the Gold Coast waterway, the Brisbane corridor and the Moreton Bay islands.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR (H2 2026+) could extend to longer SE-Queensland coastal trunks (e.g. toward the Sunshine Coast).

competitive_landscape: Today road-and-marina dominated with some bay ferries; no foiling incumbent. The waterway density and Brisbane congestion create both charter and commuter cases.
seasonality: Year-round subtropical; peak Australian summer and school holidays; sheltered Broadwater operable most conditions.
regulatory_note: Australian flag; AMSA certification; Translink concessions for any SE-Queensland public-network integration; Gold Coast Waterways Authority manages the waterway.

precedents.why_it_matters: The Gold Coast mirrors Miami's dense canal-and-marina lifestyle waterway with a congested metro-corridor commuter case.
